issuer: the Chief of Police of Yap

licence.name: operator's license, class (2) (vehicles of 3,000 pounds gross or less)

note: Read 2026-11-03 on the FSM's Legal Information System (fsmlaw.org), in a browser (the site answers this client's plain fetch with Mod Security's 406). The LIS is run from the FSM Supreme Court (its office is in the Court's building in Palikir, its webmaster the Court's), and its codes are copies of the governments' official publications, as its disclaimer says, so it is read as the court's own legal register. Yap State Code, Title 25, ch. 3: § 301, a fee of $10.00 to the Chief of Police for each license (YSL 1-93 § 12); § 303(a), none to anyone under sixteen; § 304(b)(1)(A), sixteen for class (2), vehicles of 3,000 pounds gross or less; § 307(a), the Chief of Police examines each applicant before issuing a license; § 310, every operator's license is valid for three years from its date of issue (YSL 1-93 § 21). The learner's permit ($5, sixty days) isn't held; the chapter names no identification card.

sources.title: Yap State Code, Title 25 (Motor Vehicles & Highways), ch. 3 (Licensing of Operators), on the FSM Legal Information System
sources.said: § 301 ... A fee of $10.00 shall be paid to the Chief of Police for each such license issued. ... § 303 ... issued to any person: (a) Under the age of sixteen years; ... § 304 ... (a) ... (2) All vehicles not specified elsewhere in this subsection having a gross weight of 3,000 pounds or less; ... (b) ... (1) Shall have attained the age of: (A) Sixteen years, in the case of an operator's license or learner's permit issued under paragraphs (1), (2), (3), or (4) of subsection (a) of this section ... § 307 ... (a) The Chief of Police or his duly authorized representative, before issuing an operator's license, shall examine each applicant ... § 310 . Term of license . Every operator's license issued shall be valid for three years from the date of issue unless suspended or revoked as provided in Division 1 of this title.
